entry.title: Ansible From a Blank Workstation to a Deployment I Reviewed Before It Ran
entry.summary: The first assignment was the least glamorous and probably the most useful. Ansible can't run natively on Windows, so the controller lives in Ubuntu under WSL. I installed Ansible, ansible-lint, yamllint and pre-commit inside a Python virtual environment, pinned the versions in requirements.txt, and set up SSH keys, an agent, and Git hooks that lint every YAML file before a commit. Four small problems each taught me something: My project was on the Windows drive. From Linux, every file there looks world-writable, and Ansible deliberately ignores an ansible.cfg in a world-writable folder. It doesn't warn you loudly, it just runs with defaults. Moving the project into the Linux home folder fixed it. A hidden character broke the pre-commit config. I had generated a version number with a comman…

entry.title: Would you trust AI with your entire codebase?
entry.summary: Most developers trust AI to write a function. But would you trust it with your entire project? Multiple files. That's a very different problem. And that's exactly where I think AI development is heading. NullCry is my attempt at building for that direction. Instead of treating every prompt as an isolated coding task, NullCry is designed to work with the project as a whole. Bring your own API key. I'm not claiming AI can replace developers. I'm asking whether AI should be treated as a code generator at all. Maybe the better model is an AI that works alongside the entire project. Would you trust an AI with your codebase? Yes or no — and why? — Omar Zahouri https://nullcry.com

entry.title: Downtime Monitoring for SaaS Applications with Multiple Microservices — Signal Design
entry.summary: Short answer: Downtime monitoring for SaaS applications with multiple microservices works best as layered evidence: service heartbeats, a synthetic checkout journey, and probes from multiple regions, interpreted together before anyone declares the application down. The least complex design that gives a trustworthy answer is layered. A checkout monitor should answer one operational question: can a customer complete the purchase right now? Treat each result as a signal, then interpret the signals together before declaring the checkout down. That last step matters. A payment service can be healthy while an API gateway, inventory dependency, or browser-facing path is failing. A single green endpoint is not proof that checkout works; a single red dependency is not automatically a customer-visib…

entry.title: I built an AI developer tool with almost no money.
entry.summary: I didn't start NullCry with a team. I didn't have investors. I didn't have a big marketing budget. I had an idea, a browser, and a lot of time. I wanted to build something I would actually use as a developer: An AI tool that works with the project itself, not just isolated pieces of code. So I built NullCry. Today it can work across multiple files, continue existing projects, make cross-file changes, fix problems, and generate complete projects. The interesting part? I'm still building it independently. No big company behind it. Just one developer trying to see how far the idea can go. Maybe it will succeed. But I think independent developers should build ambitious things anyway. So I'm putting NullCry in front of the developer community. If you were building this from zero, what would you change first? — Omar Zahouri https://nullcry.com

entry.summary: I built a booking app for gyms with React, TanStack Start and Supabase. The part that looked easy and wasn't: two people booking the same slot at the same moment. This post explains the approach I ended up with, with a simplified version of the code. The problem A client opens the booking page, picks a service, a date and a time slot. entry.title: SonicWall CVE-2026-19868: SSL-VPN SAML MFA Bypass Exploited in the Wild

what: SonicWall disclosed CVE-2026-19868, an SSL-VPN authentication bypass in SonicOS that lets attackers with valid credentials for an alternate authentication method skip SAML controls, and CISA has confirmed it is exploited in the wild. impact: On SAML-configured SSL-VPN deployments, the SAML-enforced MFA layer can be sidestepped, turning a single stolen password into remote network access. fix: Upgrade to SonicOS 7.3.4-7013 (Gen7) or 8.2.3-8015 (Gen8), which fix CVE-2026-19868 and six other flaws; SonicWall says no workarounds exist. who: Organizations running SonicOS Gen7 7.3.3-7015 and earlier or Gen8 8.2.2-8015 and earlier with SSL-VPN configured for SAML authentication. entry.title: I don't think developers need another AI chatbot.
entry.summary: I don't think developers need another AI chatbot. We already have enough of them. What developers need is AI that can actually work with the software they're building. Not just: "Write me a function." But: "Here is my project. Understand it. Change these files. Fix what breaks. Continue from where we stopped. Keep the whole thing working." That's the idea behind NullCry. NullCry is an AI project development tool designed to work across real projects and multiple files. You bring your own API key. No login. I'm building it independently, and I'm deliberately challenging the way AI development tools are being packaged today. Maybe the idea is wrong. Maybe developers don't want this. If you disagree, tell me exactly why. I'd rather get a brutal technical opinion than another "looks cool." — Omar Zahouri https://nullcry.com
